title: Acyclicity and square-zero kernel for the almost blowup square of an equation in two generators
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter flat.tex (More on Flatness), section 'The local structure of a finite type module'
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file flat.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: For an almost blowup square Z, X, X', E attached to two equations f_1, f_2 the lemma asserts that H^p(X', O_{X'}) vanishes for p > 0 and that the restriction Gamma(X, O_X) -> Gamma(X', O_{X'}) is surjective with kernel an ideal of square zero (statement lines 11781-11788). The proof computes first in the universal case A = Z[f_1, f_2], where X' turns out to be the effective Cartier divisor in P^1_X cut out by the global section f_2T_0 - f_1T_1, giving the resolution 0 -> O(-1) -> O -> O_{X'} -> 0 and hence the vanishing and the isomorphism of global sections from the standard cohomology of the projective line (proof lines 11791-11809). The passage to an arbitrary A is a base change argument that invokes the three fibrewise H^1 and H^0 vanishing lemmas (proof lines 11812-11820). The kernel computation is separate and concrete: an element a of A killed on X' is written on the two affine charts as (f_1x - f_2) times a polynomial in x and as (f_1 - f_2y) times a polynomial in y, which yields the chain a = f_2a_0, f_1a_0 = f_2a_1, ..., f_1a_r = 0 and the symmetric chain for the b's, and multiplying two such systems gives aa' = f_1f_2a_0b'_0 = f_1f_2a_1b'_1 = ... = 0 (proof lines 11823-11843). Recognising the two chart presentations as the source of the square-zero statement is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
